text: {"facts":[{"statement":"The input has lowercase text on the first line and a pattern on the second; both lengths are between 1 and 200000.","source_ids":["task"]},{"statement":"Count text windows whose length equals the pattern length and whose letters can be rearranged to match the pattern, with each '?' matching any lowercase letter; output 0 if the pattern is longer than the text.","source_ids":["task"]},{"statement":"For text \"a\" and pattern \"aa\", the expected output is 0.","source_ids":["public1"]},{"statement":"For text \"accaab\" and pattern \"aaabac\", the expected output is 0.","source_ids":["public2"]}],"open_requirements":["Determine an efficient way to count all qualifying windows within the stated length limit.","Clarify implementation details for handling wildcard characters while checking a window."],"tentative_options":[{"id":"fixed-count-sliding-window","method":"Maintain letter frequencies for the current window and compare them against the pattern's fixed-letter frequencies; a window qualifies when every fixed-letter requirement is met, since the remaining positions can be covered by wildcards.","unverified_assumptions":["The pattern's '?' characters are independent wildcards that can match any lowercase letter."]},{"id":"deficit-sliding-window","method":"Maintain per-letter deficits between the pattern's fixed letters and the current window as a fixed-length window slides; count windows in which no fixed-letter deficit remains.","unverified_assumptions":["A window with at least the required count of every fixed pattern letter can assign all remaining positions to the wildcards."]}],"possible_checks":["Test the stated examples, including the case where the pattern is longer than the text.","Compare a sliding-window implementation against direct enumeration on small texts and patterns, including patterns containing only wildcards."]}
